debts.summary: Shell summon, toggle, and hide accept a plugin id plus opaque JSON but no typed invoking screen, connector/EDID, anchor rectangle, seat, or focus-restoration target.
debts.impact: Multi-monitor placement and dismissal behavior depends on component-local or default-screen state and cannot be reproduced by another caller.
debts.exitCondition: Every invocation is a typed v0-or-later envelope and VM proofs cover monitor hotplug, reopen placement, anchor selection, seat routing, and focus restoration.

debts.summary: Bar-widget surface summons select the first loaded widget instance instead of the widget on the invoking screen.
debts.impact: The same route can open on the wrong monitor when bars exist on more than one screen.
debts.exitCondition: The shell resolves a supplied screen identity and anchor to one deterministic per-screen surface owner and preserves that owner across reopen.

debts.summary: Transient focus capture and restoration are component-specific; most surfaces do not retain an explicit restoration target.
debts.impact: Dismissal can return focus inconsistently and callers cannot distinguish deliberate click-through from lost focus.
debts.exitCondition: All transient routes consume the shared focus-restoration contract and prove close, toggle, launch, click-through, and target-disappearance cases.

debts.summary: Taskbar identity lowercases desktop ids and compositor classes and then uses substring and Chromium special-case matching.
debts.impact: Pins, running groups, icons, recent items, notifications, and app records can split or collide, especially for web apps.
debts.exitCondition: A checked application registry joins exact desktop entry, StartupWMClass/app id, launch token, notification identity, and installed record with explicit aliases only.

debts.summary: Standalone product apps receive separate Fabric sessions, but every same-user RPC client is currently admitted through the shared fabric.owner-rpc endpoint role and the caller-supplied client label carries no authority.
debts.impact: Settings and Agent Center cannot yet receive distinct grants or be authenticated as their reserved stable product principals.
debts.exitCondition: Daemon-owned endpoint admission binds each packaged product process to its reserved principal without trusting a caller-supplied label, and spoofing tests prove another same-user process cannot claim that role.

debts.summary: Start, Run, and the system menu each build private result objects without the normalized identity, provenance, trust, typed action, route, and rank contract.
debts.impact: Search sources cannot be safely merged and consumers cannot explain why a result exists or which authority will execute it.
debts.exitCondition: All product search producers emit the normalized result schema and golden tests prove stable ranking, provenance, and typed actions across consumers.

debts.summary: Menu search can expose command-backed mutations that have no capability id, normalized preflight, or operation record.
debts.impact: A result can bypass the human/agent same-path rule and its provenance does not establish mutation authority.
debts.exitCondition: Normalized search imports a mutating action only when it references a registered capability and visible human route; legacy commands remain excluded until converted.

debts.summary: Consumer QML still owns Process, execDetached, raw hyprctl, and command construction at thirty-seven checked source paths.
debts.impact: Mutation validation, cancellation, operation identity, authorization, errors, and recovery are fragmented across UI code.
debts.exitCondition: The checked direct-execution inventory is empty for consumer UI and every mutation resolves through a typed provider capability.

debts.summary: All first-party and enabled third-party QML executes inside one Quickshell process and therefore one shared shell principal.
debts.impact: A UI component cannot be treated as an independently authenticated process owner or granted standing consequential authority.
debts.exitCondition: Standalone applications and provider endpoints have process/session-bound principals, while the shared shell retains no standing high-risk grants.

debts.summary: Current Quickshell IPC targets accept calls without an endpoint-bound product principal or typed invocation envelope.
debts.impact: Target and method identify code to call but do not establish caller role, route provenance, approval scope, or monitor/focus context.
debts.exitCondition: Product mutation and surface routes enter through endpoint/session-bound Fabric principals and typed contracts; heritage IPC is read-only or explicitly legacy.
